test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following does NOT support rural development?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Urban credit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Urban credit **is primarily directed towards **urban areas **and does not directly contribute to rural development.
 
• Rural development focuses on improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas, often through initiatives such as organic farming, marketing development, and human resource development.
 
• Urban credit facilities are designed to cater to the **financial needs of urban populations **and typically involve different **financial instruments and support structures **compared to rural credit facilities.
 
• While urban credit can indirectly affect rural areas through urban-rural linkages, it is not a direct measure for rural development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Promotion of organic farming**

 
 
• Organic farming **promotes sustainable agricultural practices **that are beneficial for the environment and rural communities.
 
• It helps in improving soil health, reducing pollution, and increasing biodiversity.
 
• Farmers practicing organic farming often receive premium prices for their produce, which can enhance their income and livelihood.
 
 
 
• **Development of marketing**
 
 
• Effective marketing strategies are crucial for rural development as they help farmers and rural producers get better prices for their products.
 
• Development of rural marketing infrastructure, such as storage facilities and transportation, can significantly improve market access for rural communities.
 
 
 
• **Development of human resources**
 
 
• Investing in education and skill development in rural areas is essential for empowering rural populations.
 
• Human resource development initiatives can lead to better job opportunities and improved standards of living in rural areas.
